extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for preparing, mailing, timing, and extending responses and Office actions in ex parte reexamination proceedings under the MPEP and 37 CFR (especially 1.550). Includes examiner duties, title-change rules, transmittal/mailing, and extension-of-time standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must address prior responses in subsequent Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsequent to the first Office action, the examiner must be careful to additionally address all patent owner responses to previous actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner concludes in any Office action that one or more of the claims are patentable over the cited patents or printed publications, the examiner should indicate why the claim(s) is clearly patentable in a manner similar to that used to indicate reasons for allowance (MPEP § 1302.14). If the record is clear why the claim(s) is/are clearly patentable, the examiner may refer to the particular portions of the record which clearly establish the patentability of the claim(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: First action must respond to substance of each argument (37 CFR 1.510/1.530/1.535)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first action should also respond to the substance of each argument raised by the patent owner and requester pursuant to 37 CFR 1.510, 1.530, and 1.535.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If arguments are presented which are inappropriate in reexamination, they should be treated in accordance with 37 CFR 1.552(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent owner statements (37 CFR 1.501(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If any statement of the patent owner submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) is relied upon in the detailed explanation, requester must have explained how that statement is being used to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim in connection with prior art applied to that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That explanation will be considered by the Office, when drafting the Office action, in determining the scope of the claims of the patent which are subject to reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness of examiner's action due to finality
rubrics_metrics.description: It is especially important that the examiner’s action in reexamination be thorough and complete in view of the finality of a reexamination proceeding and the patent owner’s inability to file a continuation proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title change procedures in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, the title will not need to be changed during reexamination. If a change of the title is necessary, patent owner should be notified of the need to provide an amendment changing the title as early as possible in the prosecution as a part of an Office Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all of the claims are found to be patentable and a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate has been or is to be mailed, a change to the title of the invention by the examiner may only be done by a formal Examiner’s Amendment. Changing the title and merely initialing the change is NOT permitted in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of discussions/conferences to place proceeding in condition for NIRC
rubrics_metrics.description: Current procedure permits the examiner, in the exercise of his or her professional judgment to indicate that a discussion with the patent owner’s representative may result in agreement whereby the reexamination proceeding may be placed in condition for issuing a Notice of Intent to Issue a Reexamination Certificate (NIRC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this practice the patent owner’s representative can be adequately prepared to conduct such a discussion. Any resulting amendment may be made either by the patent owner’s attorney or agent, or by the examiner in an examiner’s amendment. When extensive amendments are necessary, it is preferable if the amendments were filed by the patent owner’s attorney or agent of record since this will provide the file wrapper with a better record because the amendments would include the patent owner’s arguments for patentability as required by 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference sign-off when preliminary decision reached
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s preliminary decision to reject and/or allow the claims, the Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner, with the two or more other conferees initialing the action (as “conferee”) to indicate their presence in the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing Office action — panel review conference (MPEP §2271.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a patent owner response to the action by the CRU, or upon the expiration of the time to submit the response, the examiner will be notified. The examiner will prepare for and set up a panel review conference as per MPEP § 2271.01, to discuss the issuance of the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may prepare the Office action after the conference, or may prepare the Office action prior to the conference and revise it as needed after the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened two-month statutory response period (generally)
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period of two months will generally be set for filing a response to an Office action in an ex parte reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An extension of time may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). See MPEP § 2265 for extension procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing and correspondence address rules for Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexamination forms are structured so that the identifying information for the reexamination file and the correspondence address for the patent owner ... can be printed on the forms. Usually, the official correspondence address of the patent owner, which is of record in the file of the patent, is the mailing address of the patent owner's legal representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no official correspondence address of record, the Office may treat the mailing address of the patent owner as the correspondence address. Where multiple owners, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first named patent owner as the correspondence address. The Office will not engage in double correspondence with more than one patent owner. Copies of Office actions may be obtained via Public PAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal form PTOL-465 and delivery to third party requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: All actions in a third party requester ex parte reexamination will have a copy mailed to the third party requester. A transmittal form PTOL-465 must be used in providing the third party requester with a copy of each Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one third party requester and a requester has not designated a registered patent practitioner address, the Office may treat the mailing address of the first named third party requester as the correspondence address. A completed PTOL-465 will be provided as needed and the number of transmittal forms provides a reference for number of copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.136 extensions not permitted in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(a) and (b) are NOT applicable to ex parte reexamination proceedings under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ex parte reexamination proceeding does not involve an 'application' or an 'applicant' for purposes of 1.136. Extensions in ex parte reexamination are requested pursuant to 37 CFR 1.550(c) and require the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for extension of time (37 CFR 1.17(g)) and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(g) is the required fee for filing a request for an extension of time in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike 1.136 practice, the period of extension is not determined by the amount of the fee paid. The fee is for filing the request. Under 37 CFR 1.550(c), each request must specify the requested period of extension and must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 1.17(g). A request must be submitted as a separate paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: General extension-of-time practice (who decides; automatic two-month)
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests by the patent owner for extensions of time to respond ... must be filed under 37 CFR 1.550(c), in writing, and will be decided by the Director or SPRS of the CRU or the Director of a Technology Center (TC) conducting the reexamination proceeding, with the exception of an automatic two-month extension of time to take further action which will be granted upon filing a first timely response to a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be filed on or before the day action is due, and will be granted only for sufficient cause, except for the automatic two-month extension and the 'no cause' two-month extension in certain patent owner requested or Director ordered reexaminations. Mere filing of request will not effect extension in most cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory two-month reply by third party requester (37 CFR 1.535) cannot be extended
rubrics_metrics.description: The time period for filing a third party requester reply under 37 CFR 1.535 ... cannot be extended under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extensions will be permitted to the time for filing a reply under 37 CFR 1.535 by the requester because the two-month period for filing the reply is a statutory period (35 U.S.C. 304). A statutory period for response cannot be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party requested ex parte reexamination extension practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The extension of time practice under 37 CFR 1.550(c) for patent owner responses in an ex parte reexamination proceeding which has been requested by a third party remains unchanged under the rules and practices adopted in view of the Patent Law Treaty (PLT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A third party requested ex parte reexamination is initiated by a party other than the patent owner or the Office; PLT minimum reply provisions do not apply. The patent owner must file a written request specifying the requested period for extension, and must file the request, the required fee, and the response within the specified period for extension. A request may be filed with or without the response. Any request in a third party requested reexamination must include a showing of sufficient cause and be for a reasonable time. First requests will generally be granted if sufficient cause is shown (usually one month); second/subsequent requests only in extraordinary situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'No cause' extensions up to two months for patent owner requested or Director ordered reexaminations
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective Dec 18, 2013, 37 CFR 1.550(c) was amended to omit the requirement ... for a showing of sufficient cause in a request for an extension of time for up to two months from the time period set in the Office action, i.e., a 'no cause' extension, in patent owner requested or Director ordered ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner must timely file: (i) a written request specifying the requested period (up to two months), filed as a separate paper; and (ii) the fee set forth in 1.17(g). The written request and fee may be filed with or without the response, but the request, fee, and response must all be timely filed. The Office may then grant an extension up to two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of more than two months require sufficient cause and are rare
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension for more than two months from the time period for response set in the Office action must include a showing of sufficient cause, and the extension must be for a reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests will only be granted in extraordinary circumstances. Timely filing of a written request and the required fee alone will not result in an extension. The request must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for filing extension requests and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The day on which action by the patent owner is due is generally the day before expiration of the time period set in the Office action. Specific rules determine the latest filing dates for 'no cause' requests depending on whether the Office action set a one- or two-month period, and examples illustrate combinations of no-cause and cause-based requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: If Office action sets two-month period and patent owner requests two-month extension, request+fee+response must be filed within four months of mail date. If Office sets two-month period and requests one-month extension, file within three months. Detailed examples (5 examples) show filing permutations and consequences of untimely filings. Requests for more-than-two-month extensions can be combined with 'no cause' requests but must include showing of sufficient cause for the portion >2 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for appeals governed by 37 CFR 1.550(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time for filing a notice of appeal, an appeal brief, or a reply brief are governed by 37 CFR 1.550(c). For purposes of requesting an extension of time for an appeal brief or a reply brief, the 'time set in the Office action' is the time permitted to file the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In patent owner requested or Director ordered reexamination proceedings, the patent owner may request an extension of time for filing an appeal brief or a reply brief for up to two months from the time permitted to file the brief, without providing a showing of sufficient cause (a 'no cause' extension). Requests for more than two months require sufficient cause and are rarely granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for showing sufficient cause for extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for any extension of time ... must include a showing of sufficient cause, and the extension must be for a reasonable time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any evaluation must balance providing the patent owner a fair opportunity to present an argument and 35 U.S.C. 305 requirement that the proceeding be conducted with special dispatch. Except for 'no cause' extensions, requests must fully state reasons, include what action patent owner has taken to provide a response as of the request date, why additional time is needed despite such actions, and a factual accounting of reasonably diligent behavior by all responsible for preparing a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for extension to file petition after denial require 37 CFR 1.183
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension of the time period to file a petition from the denial of a request for reexamination can only be entertained by filing a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 with the appropriate fee to waive the time provisions of 37 CFR 1.515(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing mechanics and mailing certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension of time under 37 CFR 1.550(c) must be submitted as a separate paper which will be forwarded to the CRU SPRS or TC Director for action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate of mailing and the certificate of transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8) and the Priority Mail Express® mailing procedure (37 CFR 1.10) may be used to file a request for extension of time. The time extended is added to the last calendar day of the original period, as opposed to being added to the day it would have been due when said last day is a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday.
